observations.text: Selection, mechanical, at HEAD 9a9908a with an empty git status --porcelain. argv timeout 120 code-fact impacted-tests crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs --root /Users/jeffbailey/Projects/canzan/foundry: exit 124 (killed at the bound), stdout empty (0 bytes), stderr empty - the fourth round in a row the port tool returns no selection within a bound. Fallback, mechanical: argv git diff --name-only 60a0269 9a9908a names six paths, exit 0, of which three are code: the oracle crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature and both declared supports crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs and crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs; the other three are docs (acceptance.md, acceptance.html, handoff.json). No other test file changed by this Request's design turns, so the reviewed set is exactly the declared oracle plus its two declared supports. The design command for that oracle is scripts/test-in-lima.sh with eip_lane us-iis-07, whose runner filter at crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/acceptance.rs:296 is has("us-iis-07") && !skip_lane && !manual && !manual-trigger && !pending, with skip_lane false for a non-eip tag: the @needs-matrix and @iis-replica rows of this slice are therefore included, not skipped.

typesafe: unavailable. argv timeout 120 python3 /Users/jeffbailey/.claude/skills/nw-typesafe-system-one/scripts/jev_decide.py --request - --output - run from a shell command with the request on stdin (three reviewer-owned noul questions over a redacted state: whether the oracle's workspace-page observations falsify a product that leaves a discarded connection reading as connected; whether its instance-page observations falsify a product that does not ask for the Slack app again after starting over; whether the healthy-key post row tells a product that discards there from one that changes nothing, despite its recorded missing-confirmation limitation): exit 3, stdout "typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment...)", stderr empty. No producer-owned judgment was consumed. All three questions were resolved locally from the oracle bytes, the shipped locked copy and the support step bodies, and are recorded as observations below. A capability limit of this review, not a judgment.

The one non-blocking finding carried out of the S2 review is discharged by this oracle, by its first remediation. The healthy-key row at crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1347-1366 now adds, after its GET half, "When Priya posts a start over request anyway" with five Thens: the answer is this Foundry's integrations page, the stored secrets key and the Activity are as they were, nothing read there says "Secrets key generated.", Canzan Labs' saved Slack connection still opens, and the saved Slack app is still in effect with its secrets and its activity unchanged. The post step is the shipped regex at crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:188, whose support when_post_door (support line 1044) calls remember for StartOver, and remember (support line 2678) captures the stored key through the test seam, the whole Activity list and the config version, which then_nothing_replaced (support line 2794) compares one by one - so "as they were" spans the version every replica follows, which the declared Expected names. The POST of that door is a recorded S3 target (architecture.md route-table impact, crates/foundry-app/src/lib.rs:855), so unlike in S2 the row is inside this slice's targets and no 405 stands in for the behaviour. The S3 acceptance row at docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md records both halves in its stimulus ("A kept link asks for the start over address, and a stale tab posts to it") and its expected text, with its own disposition note naming the residual limit: this post carries no typed confirmation, so a Foundry refusing it only for the missing Confirmation is not told apart here. That limit is honest and bounded - under a healthy key no I-28 page exists to answer, so the assertion on the ordinary integrations page still fails a Foundry that answers a confirm page or discards anything.

Forward closure, declared obligation to falsifiable observation, read off the oracle bytes. P8's apply: the main row asserts the I-21 notice once, the landed address carrying no notice, the stored key read through the declared test seam (then_key_started_over, support line 3330, where generated_secrets_key at crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_seam.rs returns Some only when the unwrapped key's id equals the stored key id - which is the falsifier "the stored key check names a different key than the stored key"), and the reload reading no notice. P8's refusals: the outline's empty and lower-case rows and the live-opener row each answer the start over page with the I-28 question (then_on_start_over_page, support line 3066, asserts success, the door's own address and the I-28 question text) and assert the stored key, the whole Activity and the config version unchanged, then restore the instance key and read every remaining credential opening. P5 and T2: the main row asserts the three Activity lines in order, the started-over line byte for byte with its count of 3, which is the contract obligation that the persisted action renders as its I-18 Deliverable B words and not an underscore fallback. P9: the main row asserts the workspace page reads no connection as connected (then_no_connection_connected, support line 3350, refuses both "Connected to " and "Connected as "), offers to connect Matrix, and reads the locked W-2 sentence "Slack is not set up on this Foundry yet. An instance operator adds the Foundry Slack app once." - the same bytes the shipped rows at integrations-wayfinding.feature:154 and instance-integration-setup.feature:169 already assert - plus, on the instance page, the stored key as set and the I-5 ask for the Slack app again. P10 with L11/F159: the rotate row asserts exit 0 and the 0-credential report (then_rotated), the re-entered app still in effect with both secrets and with Slack's events still verifying under the saved signing secret (then_saved_app_unchanged, support line 1664, which posts Slack's challenge signed with SIGNING_SECRET), and the page reading the key as set. P12: the main row is that scenario, cost read first with nothing changed, then the apply and the workspace page. L3/F114: the live-opener row makes the other server quiet for a minute, reads the offer, then has it speak again before the confirm, waiting on that server's own beat record (when_other_server_speaks_again, support line 3385, await_beats) rather than on a sleep. L1/F100, L1/F101, L7/F134: the two order rows, replacement after start over and start over after replacement, each assert the offer pair after the apply and that what was saved in between keeps opening. The trimmed-confirmation row maps to the declared design decision at architecture.md:82 and architecture.md:1003 (StartOverConfirmation::typed trims surrounding whitespace, case-sensitive), so it is not an invented requirement.

Reverse closure and craft discipline. Every observation the eight new cases make is traceable to a declared promise, law or locked copy: the I-21 notice, its read-once and the Activity lines to P8 and P5 with T2; the workspace-page lines to P9 in the W-2 and K-2 words the scope locks unchanged; the rotate report to P10 and L11; the offer pairs to L7; the live-opener refusal to L3; the trimming to the design decision at architecture.md:82; the no-lost-marking and no-email clauses to the S3 Expected text and L2; "the new secrets key appears nowhere Priya reads" to KPI-IIS-G1. None of them pins a private field, a mock call or documentation prose, and the only non-HTTP reader is the generated-key test seam that DISTILL D6 and check-arch integrations-test-seam declare. The step DSL stays business-worded: every new step body is one call into the support module (steps lines 756-783), the new support helpers carry WHAT/WHY/HOW failure messages, and TypedForm (support line 3228) reads the Confirmation field's name off the page the product draws rather than spelling it in a scenario, so no scenario couples to a field name. No scenario is parameterized beyond the two-row confirmation outline, whose rows share one outcome shape. The new Given "Priya has started over with a new secrets key" drives the same public form the When drives, so the two order rows and the rotate row need no fixture back door. Three capability or scope limits stay explicit, each recorded on its own S3 acceptance row: the falsifier half "a credential this Foundry can open being discarded" is unobservable in this state, because under I-26 every credential form is withheld and no credential this server opens can exist (the replacement rows carry that half); L3's inside-the-transaction half is carried by the Quint model, the acceptance row observing only the GET-to-POST window; and the healthy-key post carries no typed Confirmation. No timing finding is claimed: this review measured no per-test time, which the default budgets do not require, and no row is at or above half a budget by any measurement taken here.

Two weak clauses, read and judged non-blocking, neither hiding a missing obligation. First, the last Then of "A start over after a replacement leads back to a Foundry whose key can be replaced" asserts that Canzan Labs' workspace integrations page offers to connect Matrix, while that row's Given holds one Slack connection and the saved app and never connects Matrix: the offer is present in that state whether or not the start over ran, so the clause discriminates nothing there. It is faithful to the declared S3 expected text, and the same promise is observed non-vacuously in the main row, where Canzan Labs is connected to Matrix first and the page must offer the connection again after the discard, so nothing is lost. Second, the Matrix-ready half of E21 is observed on the workspace page's offer rather than as a line on the instance page; the instance page carries no Matrix setup line, Matrix needing no instance app, so there is no instance-page observation to make. Neither clause is a defect of this phase and neither is recorded as a finding.

Measured RED, new execution in this review at HEAD 9a9908a with a clean tree (only this reviewer's nwdes draft directory is untracked). argv: timeout -k 30 2400 scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c 'mkdir -p ~/.cache/rustc-tmp; export TMPDIR=$HOME/.cache/rustc-tmp CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4; source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-07'; exit 101 (the lane's own), stdout kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/ae6f0864-8ca5-43d5-b970-fb78c37ae831/scratchpad/lane-us-iis-07.S3.txt, 718 lines, stderr merged into it. The command first waited about seven minutes on the shared VM test lock, held by another project's coverage run in the same Lima VM, then warmed the release binary (eip_warm: release build finished in 1m40s, --help answered in 0s) and built the acceptance crate in 8m24s. Result: 29 scenarios (20 passed, 9 failed), 451 steps (442 passed, 9 failed), 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s), lane exit 101 at crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/acceptance.rs:399. The 29 cases are the 20 @us-iis-07 declarations expanded by the two confirmation example rows and the shipped outlines, which is the 21 cases of the S2 run plus this slice's 8 new cases - counted mechanically off the feature bytes before the run and matched by the run. All nine failures are semantic for the missing Start over apply, none scaffolding: every one reads "/admin/instance/integrations/secrets-key/start-over answered 405 Method Not Allowed", the POST method absent from the route this slice's targets register (crates/foundry-app/src/lib.rs route-table impact), reached through the product's own form with a valid form token on a page the product drew and answered 200. grep -c over the run: 9 occurrences of 405, 0 of 404, 9 of the failure glyph, so no case fails for another cause. The nine are the main apply row, the trimmed-confirmation row, the two confirmation outline rows, the live-opener row, the start-over-after-a-replacement row (each on its promised business observation: the I-21 words, or the I-28 page answered again), and the two order/rotation rows whose public Given cannot be established (message "precondition: Priya started over with a new secrets key from the start over page"), plus the healthy-key row's new POST half. Unlike the revision S2 refused, no 405 here stands outside the slice's targets: the healthy-key row's GET half passes in this run (lines 491-513: the integrations page answered, the stored key and the Activity as they were, the saved connection still opening), and only its POST half is RED, on the method this slice adds. All 11 shipped S1 cases and all 10 S2 cases except that extended one pass, so the S3 oracle regresses nothing and the S2 craft is green under it.

diagnostic:
Accepted at the DISTILL S3 oracle phase, before craft, at HEAD 9a9908a with a clean tree. No finding: nothing blocks craft and nothing is carried as a non-blocking defect.

Closure holds in both directions. Every declared S3 obligation has a constructible stimulus, expected observation and falsifier through the public driving port: P8's apply (I-21 read once, the landed address carrying no notice, the stored key read through the declared generated-key seam, whose reader returns a key only when the stored key check names that same key), P8's three refusals (empty, lower case, and a server that speaks again between the page and the button, each answered the I-28 page with the stored key, the whole Activity list and the config version unchanged, then every remaining credential opening once the instance key is restored), P5 with the T2 contract obligation (the three Activity lines in order, the started-over line byte for byte with its count), P9 (no connection reading as connected, Matrix offered again, and the locked W-2 sentence this feature's shipped rows already assert), P10 with L11/F159 (exit 0, no credential re-sealed, Slack's events still verifying under the saved signing secret), P12, L3/F114, and L1/L7's two orders. Nothing the oracle asserts is outside a declared promise, law or locked copy; the trimmed confirmation maps to the design's own decision that only the trimmed text START OVER is admitted.

The one non-blocking finding carried out of the S2 review is discharged by its first remediation: the healthy-key row now posts the start-over address as a stale tab would and asserts the ordinary integrations page with the stored key, the whole Activity and the version every replica follows as they were, no I-21 read, the saved connection still opening and the saved app still in effect. Its POST is a recorded S3 target, so unlike in S2 the row can reach green inside the slice, and the S3 acceptance row records both halves with its own residual limit.

Measured RED, a new execution in this review: 29 scenarios (20 passed, 9 failed), 451 steps (442 passed, 9 failed), 0 parsing and 0 hook errors, lane exit 101. All nine failures are semantic for the missing apply - every one on the start-over door answering 405 Method Not Allowed, the POST this slice's route-table target registers, reached through the product's own form with a valid token on a page the product drew and answered. No 404, no import, fixture, collection or setup failure, and no 405 outside the slice's targets: the healthy-key row's GET half passes and only its new POST half is RED. All shipped S1 and S2 cases pass under the new bytes.

Three limits stay explicit rather than hidden, each on its own S3 acceptance row: the falsifier half "a credential this Foundry can open being discarded" is unreachable in this state, because under I-26 every credential form is withheld, so no credential this server opens can exist (the replacement rows carry that half); L3's inside-the-transaction half is carried by the Quint model with its m5 gate-only-at-the-GET mutant, the acceptance row observing the GET-to-POST window; and the healthy-key post carries no typed Confirmation, so a Foundry refusing it only for that is not told apart there. Two clauses are weak and recorded as such, neither hiding an obligation: the Matrix offer in the start-over-after-a-replacement row discriminates nothing in a state where Matrix was never connected, and the Matrix-ready half is observed on the workspace page because the instance page carries no Matrix line.

Capability limits of this review: typesafe unavailable (exit 3, the key absent from this process environment), so the three reviewer-owned questions were resolved locally from the oracle bytes, the shipped locked copy and the support step bodies; and the port selector again returned no selection within its bound (exit 124, empty output), so selection fell back to the mechanical diff, which names the declared oracle and both declared supports and no other test file. No timing measurement was taken and none is required at these budgets. Craft may start on the S3 targets; the oracle's GREEN and the promised live observations remain completion obligations.
